mechanisms.name: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS) / Sepsis
mechanisms.description: A dysregulated host response to infection or injury, characterized by widespread inflammation leading to endothelial dysfunction, vasodilation, capillary leak, and potentially organ failure. In severe cases, it progresses to septic shock.

mechanisms.name: Cardiovascular Dysfunction / Shock
mechanisms.description: Impairment of cardiac function or systemic circulation, leading to inadequate tissue perfusion and oxygen delivery. This can result from various causes including sepsis, hemorrhage, myocardial infarction, or cardiomyopathy.

mechanisms.name: Respiratory Failure / Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
mechanisms.description: Inability of the lungs to adequately oxygenate blood or eliminate carbon dioxide. ARDS is a severe form characterized by diffuse alveolar damage, pulmonary edema, and refractory hypoxemia.

mechanisms.name: Renal Dysfunction / Acute Kidney Injury (AKI)
mechanisms.description: Sudden decrease in kidney function, leading to the accumulation of waste products and fluid imbalance. Often caused by ischemia, toxins, or inflammatory processes.

mechanisms.name: Metabolic Derangement
mechanisms.description: Disruptions in metabolic processes, including glucose metabolism, acid-base balance, and electrolyte abnormalities, often secondary to critical illness or organ dysfunction.

mechanisms.name: Neurological Impairment
mechanisms.description: Compromise of brain function, ranging from altered mental status to coma. Can be caused by hypoxia, ischemia, infection, or metabolic disturbances.

mechanisms.name: Hematological Abnormalities
mechanisms.description: Disorders affecting blood cells and coagulation, contributing to oxygen carrying capacity, infection risk, and bleeding/thrombosis.

mechanisms.name: Liver Dysfunction
mechanisms.description: Impairment of liver function, affecting metabolism, detoxification, and synthetic processes.

mechanisms.name: Coagulation Dysfunction / DIC
mechanisms.description: Systemic activation of coagulation leading to microvascular thrombosis and consumption of clotting factors, often associated with sepsis or trauma.

mechanisms.name: Underlying Comorbidities and Risk Factors
mechanisms.description: Pre-existing conditions or patient characteristics that increase the risk of critical illness and mortality.
